content: 1. Cefprozil and S. pyogenes infections: Cefprozil is effective against infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. For adults, the recommended dosage is 500 mg orally once daily for 10 days, or 250–500 mg orally every 12 hours for 10 days. In cases of renal impairment (creatinine clearance <30 mL/min), the dose should be reduced to half of the usual amount. 2. Pediatric dosing for S. pyogenes infections: For children aged 6 months to 12 years, the recommended dosage is 30 mg/kg/day divided into two doses every 12 hours for 10 days. Alternatively, for children aged 2–12 years, 15–20 mg/kg/day can be administered once daily or divided into two doses every 12 hours for 10 days. 3. Spectrum of activity: Cefprozil has a spectrum of activity similar to cefuroxime and is commonly used for respiratory tract infections and otitis media. It is effective against organisms such as Bacteroides fragilis, Clostridium perfringens, Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus pyogenes. 4. Interaction with live bacterial vaccines: Cefprozil decreases the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine, through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic therapy. Similarly, the cholera vaccine should not be co-administered with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may inactivate the vaccine strain. Patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination should not receive the cholera vaccine. 5. Interaction with microbiota-based therapies: Cefprozil may reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota therapies, which contain bacterial spores, by decreasing their activity. Antibiotic regimens should be completed 2–4 days before initiating microbiota-based treatments. 6. Interaction with typhoid vaccine: Cefprozil reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of the vaccine should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic therapy. 7. Nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity with aminoglycosides: Cefprozil increases the nephrotoxic and ototoxic effects of aminoglycosides such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, plazomicin, streptomycin, and tobramycin. Caution is advised, and patients should be closely monitored when these drugs are co-administered. 8. Interaction with immune checkpoint inhibitors: Cefprozil may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors, including atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, cosibelimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab. Caution and monitoring are recommended during co-administration. 9. Interaction with hormonal contraceptives: Cefprozil may reduce the efficacy of oral hormonal contraceptives, such as those containing ethinyl estradiol, dienogest, estradiol valerate, levonorgestrel, and mestranol, by altering intestinal flora. Although the risk of contraceptive failure is low, additional or alternative forms of birth control may be advisable during concurrent use. 10. Interaction with diuretics: Cefprozil may increase the levels or effects of diuretics such as furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, methyclothiazide, and bendroflumethiazide by competing for renal tubular clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Interaction with salicylates and related drugs: Cefprozil may increase the levels or effects of salicylates (non-ASA), aspirin, choline magnesium trisalicylate, and sulfasalazine by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown, but caution is recommended. 12. Interaction with warfarin: Cefprozil may enhance the effects of warfarin through an unspecified mechanism. Patients should be closely monitored for signs of increased anticoagulation. 13. Interaction with sodium picosulfate: Cefprozil may reduce the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Caution is advised during co-administration. 14. Interaction with aspirin and related compounds: Cefprozil may increase the levels or effects of aspirin (oral, rectal), aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate, and willow bark by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown, but caution is recommended. 15. Interaction with rose hips: Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of cefprozil by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 16. Interaction with temocillin: Co-administration of cefprozil and temocillin may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Patients should be closely monitored. 17. Interaction with voclosporin: Co-administration of cefprozil and voclosporin may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 18. Interaction with aspirin and citric acid combinations: Cefprozil may increase the levels or effects of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is recommended. 19. Interaction with chloramphenicol: Chloramphenicol may reduce the efficacy of cefprozil through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 20. Interaction with warfarin: Cefprozil may enhance the effects of warfarin through an unspecified mechanism. Patients should be closely monitored for signs of increased anticoagulation.
